source: Parallel capacitances add, and series capacitances combine by reciprocals, the opposite of resistors.
Students add series capacitances directly, as they would series resistors.
Circuits often combine several capacitors. The rules look like the ones for resistors, but switched: the series rule for capacitors is the parallel rule for resistors, and the other way around.

In parallel, each capacitor has the same voltage and their charges add: $Q = C_1V + C_2V$, so $C_{\text{eq}} = C_1 + C_2$. It is like making the plates bigger. In series, the inner plates are connected only to each other, so the charge they hold is pulled across from one to the other: every capacitor carries the same charge $Q$. Their voltages add: $V = \dfrac{Q}{C_1} + \dfrac{Q}{C_2}$, so $\dfrac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2}$. It is like making the gap wider.

Parallel: $C_{\text{eq}} = C_1 + C_2 + \cdots$ (same $V$, charges add). Series: $\dfrac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \cdots$ (same $Q$, voltages add), smaller than any one of them.
The two sets of rules are mirror images.
A $3\,\mu\text{F}$ and a $6\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor in series: they hold the same charge, so the smaller one takes more of the voltage.
Find the equivalent capacitance of $3\,\mu\text{F}$ and $6\,\mu\text{F}$ in parallel, then in series.
The $3\,\mu\text{F}$ and $6\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitors are in series across $12\,\text{V}$. Find the charge and each voltage.
A $6\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is in series with a parallel pair of $2\,\mu\text{F}$ and $4\,\mu\text{F}$. Find $C_{\text{eq}}$.

Adding series capacitances directly, as you would series resistors. Putting capacitors in series is like widening the gap, which lowers capacitance. Check: a series combination is always smaller than its smallest capacitor, and a parallel one bigger than its biggest.

In series, the smaller capacitor ends up with the larger voltage, because both hold the same charge and $V = Q/C$. That is the opposite of series resistors, where the larger resistor takes the larger voltage.
